title: a worker note that GitHub would not take beside published work no longer fails the round: transient errors are retried only after a marker lookup, the note is kept with its pull request, and fm unsent lists and posts kept notes
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-04 round worker-shira-t192-r2c (T-192, existing PR #180) changed tests/board-readiness.test.sh and wrote a report in `.fm-say.md`. `post_note` (bin/fm-worker.sh:1521-1556) got gh's transient error `GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query on 2026-10-04T17:11:07Z. Please include `C81F:1B67BD:77CAE6:96A060:6AC288AB` when reporting this issue.`, so `spoke=0`. Because the round was not a rebuild, the refused-note branch at :1695-1700 did not apply, and `keep_unsent` (:1599-1602) ran at :1703-1705 and exited 73 before the normal commit and push. The EXIT trap's `publish_wip_if_dirty` (:229-267) then pushed the work as `T-192: checkpoint (exit-73)`, and the board showed a failed round. The herdr line `cleanup observation failed: Herdr command failed: pane process-info` in the same log is not the cause: bin/fm-herdr.py:1590 only labels the window and :1594 returns the run's own exit 0. Nothing reads `state/unsent/` after it is written (15 files there today, none with a pull request number recorded). This task makes a note that could not be posted beside real work a recoverable side issue instead of a failed round, while retrying only after a lookup that finds no copy of it (a lookup can lag GitHub's store, so this narrows the risk of a second copy rather than proving there is none).

No blind retry. A refusal can come back for a comment GitHub stored (the existing rule, bin/fm-worker.sh:1688-1694 and design §5.3.3). So every note this script posts carries an invisible marker line appended to the posted body (not to the kept file): `<!-- fm-note sha256=<hex> -->`, where `<hex>` is the sha256 of the note file's bytes. A new helper `note_landed <pr> <hex>` in bin/fm-worker.sh asks GitHub whether a comment on that PR already contains the marker: `"${GH:-${FM_GH:-gh}}" api "<endpoint>" --paginate --jq '.[].body'`, where the endpoint follows the existing REST rule at bin/fm-config.sh:1027-1029 (REST calls do not accept `--repo`): `repos/$GH_REPO/issues/<pr>/comments` when `FM_EXTERNAL=1`, and the `repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<pr>/comments` placeholders (resolved from the task worktree as cwd) only for the legacy self project, as bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py:26 and bin/fm-review.sh:583 already do. It returns 0 when found, 1 when not found, 2 when the lookup itself failed. The marker line, `note_landed` and the retry below apply to the self project only (`FM_EXTERNAL=0`): on an external project `post_note` behaves exactly as today (no marker, no lookup, no retry), so the `repos/$GH_REPO/...` endpoint form is used only by `bin/fm.sh unsent`'s self-only resolution and is otherwise not reached; a test asserts that an external comments-projection refusal with the transient text is offered once and makes no `gh api` call.

Bounded retry only for GitHub's transient errors, self project only. In `post_note` with `FM_EXTERNAL=0`, when `fm_comment_projection` fails and gh's stderr matches `GraphQL: Something went wrong while executing your query` or `HTTP 50[0234]`, the note is retried at most twice, after the delays in `FM_NOTE_RETRY_DELAYS` (default `2 5`, seconds; tests set `0 0`). Before each retry `note_landed` runs: found means the note landed (`spoke=1`, and the usual `ask_pass_criteria` event is emitted once); a failed lookup (2) stops retrying (treated as refused) so a duplicate is never risked. Any other refusal (no permission, 4xx, locked, a stub's generic text) is never retried, exactly as today: tests/worker-rebuild-publication.test.sh:76-95 (`rb_refusing_gh`, 'the note is offered to the pull request once') keeps passing unchanged.

Sidecar for every kept note whose pull request is known. `save_unsent` gains an optional second argument, the PR number; whenever it is given it writes the sidecar `<same name>.json` described above (with `marker` absent for notes never offered, and `head` the round's head for the 73 paths, `null` until the push for `note_unsent`). Callers pass it where known: `note_unsent`, `note_refused`/`keep_unsent` when `$PR` is set, and `lost_held` when `$PR` is set. A sidecar that cannot be written is a warning line only (`fm-worker: could not record the pull request beside <file>`): it never changes the exit status, and it never makes the run print 'it is at' for a note that was not kept (tests/worker-scratch.test.sh:25-30, where `state/unsent` is a plain file, keeps its 73 and its `assert_lacks 'it is at state/unsent'`). The evidence-retention fallback at :1503-1511 (`state/unsent/${NAME}.md`) is unchanged and has no sidecar.

Recovery command. `bin/fm.sh unsent` (new `cmd_unsent`, added to the dispatch case at about bin/fm.sh:924-939 and to `usage` at about :71) is self-project only and never takes the repository from the caller's directory. It resolves the project the way the worker does: `FM_PROJECT` unset, then `fm_storage_init "$REPO"` (bin/fm-config.sh:949-966, as bin/fm-worker.sh:45 calls it), which sets `FM_PROJECT` from `default_project` (config.yaml:72-76) and `FM_EXTERNAL` from that registry entry. If the resolved project is external (`FM_EXTERNAL=1`), `unsent` lists nothing and `--post` refuses with exit 64. Otherwise it reads `$FM_STATE_DIR/unsent/`; the projection check and the post both use that resolved entry through `fm_projection` and `fm_comment_projection` (so a self entry with `projection: local`, allowed by bin/lib/fm_registry.py:114-115, makes `--post` refuse); and every `gh` call it makes (lookup and post) runs with `$REPO` as its working directory, so the `{owner}/{repo}` placeholders resolve to the self repository. It lists every `state/unsent/*.md` in name order, one line each: file, task (from the name's `T-<n>-` or `SK-<n>-` prefix; the evidence-fallback files named `<actor>.md`, :1506, list the actor instead), saved time, and from the sidecar PR, head and round (a `head: null` sidecar lists as `not published` and `--post` skips it), or `no pull request recorded` for files without a sidecar (all 15 existing files list, unchanged on disk). `bin/fm.sh unsent --post` first checks `fm_projection` for the self project; if it is not `comments`, it refuses with exit 64 and moves nothing (a projection that would 'succeed' without posting must never mark a note posted). Otherwise it handles only entries whose sidecar has a PR: a marker lookup (the sidecar's marker, or the sha256 of the file when the sidecar has none) that finds it → moves `.md` and `.json` to `state/unsent/posted/` without posting; not found → posts the file with the marker line appended through `fm_comment_projection`, and on success moves both files to `state/unsent/posted/`; a failure leaves them in place and is reported. Nothing is deleted. `--post` is a flag with no value and no value flags are added, so tests/option-loop.test.sh's pinned fm.sh flag list (about :115-124) stays unchanged; if the implementation does add a value flag, that pin is updated in the same change.

Event consumers, every one listed. `worker_note_unsent` is added to: bin/fm-emit.sh `TYPES` (about :114-118); bin/fm-diagram.sh `ROUTINE` (about :125-129; tests/diagram.test.sh derives both lists and must stay green); design §5.1 type list (about :186-191); board/public/index.html log colour rule `.log .k-agent_lost,.log .k-reopened{color:var(--warn)}` (about :168) gains `.log .k-worker_note_unsent`; bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py `reasons` dict (about :533-535) gains `worker_note_unsent='Worker note unsent; run bin/fm.sh unsent --post'`, so the queued wake line itself (built at about :565 as `reason + ': ' + task`) tells firstmate what to run; firstmate is woken once (the wake survives an autopilot restart like the other reasons), and it is not suppressed by `busy(task)` (that suppression at about :550 lists only gate_failed, review_failed, worker_crashed). Deliberately not added: board/server.ts `STAGE` (about :226-234), so the task's lane is not moved to 'gate' for a note while its work is published; games/voyage-2d/src/board-source.js `mapped` (:5) and director.js, so the voyage shows no crash; i18n/*.json, because event summaries travel in the event itself and no i18n key exists per event type.
Scope check: every changed path is in `scope`. bin/fm-herdr.py is not changed (the misleading 'cleanup observation failed' label is out of scope and noted only).

In flight and existing data. No worker round is running when this lands (firstmate checks before merge). The 15 files already in state/unsent stay untouched: they list without a PR and `--post` skips them; none is posted automatically. Rounds started before the merge run the old code from their snapshot and may still exit 73 on a transient error; firstmate handles those by hand as today.

Ordering and overlap. Plan item 6 of state/briefs/PLAN-2026-10-05-remaining-issues.md. May be worked in parallel with the CI coverage task (T-196) and with the cursor and host/legacy tasks; it merges only after T-196 has merged and this branch has been updated onto it, so its CI covers every suite. It shares bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py (one dict line at about :533) with the ledger-removal and reload tasks; whichever merges second takes a branch update, no other overlap. `depends_on` stays empty because the ordering is enforced at merge time by firstmate.
